messages.content:
Plan:
- Implement an in-memory EventBus with publish/subscribe.
- Implement each service in its own file, each owning its own in-memory Map:
  - UserService
  - ProjectService
  - TaskService (publishes task.assigned and task.statusChanged events)
  - CommentService (publishes comment.added event)
  - NotificationService (subscribes to events and creates notifications)
- Implement a Router that handles all HTTP request routing and orchestrates calls to services, without services calling each other.
- Create main entrypoint to start the server.
- Create a demo script that starts the server and exercises the full flow.

Implementation summary:
- src/event-bus.ts: Simple in-memory pub/sub with synchronous notifications.
- src/services/user-service.ts: CRUD operations for users.
- src/services/project-service.ts: CRUD for projects and add/remove members.
- src/services/task-service.ts: CRUD for tasks, assign user (publishes task.assigned), change status with forward-only rule (publishes task.statusChanged).
- src/services/comment-service.ts: Create/list/delete comments, publish comment.added with context provided by the router for enriched payload.
- src/services/notification-service.ts: Subscribes to events and creates notifications for users. Supports listing and marking as read.
- src/router.ts: HTTP routing using Node’s http module. Parses JSON bodies, maps routes to service calls per the OpenAPI spec. Ensures forward-only transitions and 404/400 responses as appropriate.
- src/main.ts: Starts the server and exports the startServer function.
- src/demo.ts: Starts the server and demonstrates: create users → create project → add members → create tasks → assign tasks → change status → add comments → check notifications → mark notification as read → list tasks by project.

Notes on constraints:
- No direct service-to-service calls: satisfied; services do not import or call each other. Inter-service comm is via EventBus only.
- Data ownership: each service uses its own Map store.
- Single entry point: all HTTP handling is in router.ts.
- Forward-only status transitions: enforced in TaskService.changeStatus.
- No external dependencies: only Node.js built-in modules used.
- Each service in its own file: satisfied as per file structure.

How to run:
- Start server: npx tsx src/main.ts
- Run demo: npx tsx src/demo.ts
  The demo will:
  - Create Alice and Bob
  - Create project Apollo and add both as members
  - Create two tasks, assign them, change status
  - Add comments
  - Fetch notifications and mark one as read
  - List tasks by project

TypeScript compile:
- I attempted to run “npx tsc --noEmit” but the environment could not install or invoke TypeScript via npx. The code adheres to TypeScript typings and Node built-in APIs; in a normal environment with typescript and @types/node installed, it should compile cleanly.
